title: Flag future requestedAt as SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP

criteria.when: a new problem is needed for future timestamps
criteria.then: ProblemCode has a new constant SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP declared last (after CONFLICTING_REQUEST_ID) and Problem gains a static factory Problem.suspiciousTimestamp(int inputIndex, String requestId, Instant requestedAt) producing code SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP, field "requestedAt", null relatedRequestId/escalatedFrom/escalatedTo, and message "<requestId> has requestedAt <instant> in the future" using Instant.toString(), or "Request has requestedAt <instant> in the future" when requestId is null

criteria.when: validate is called on one otherwise-valid request with requestedAt 2026-10-21T08:30:00Z
criteria.then: exactly one problem is returned, with code SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP, field "requestedAt", inputIndex 0 and the request's requestId, and the request is absent from StageResult.requests()

criteria.when: requests with requestedAt 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z (exactly equal) or 2026-10-20T11:59:59.999Z are validated
criteria.then: no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem is reported and both are accepted; only an instant strictly after the clock instant is future, with no tolerance window and no configuration property

criteria.given: a request whose requestedAt is null, or whose requestedAt is listed in invalidFieldsByIndex as an unreadable raw value
criteria.when: it is validated with a fixed clock
criteria.then: only MISSING_FIELD or INVALID_VALUE for field "requestedAt" is reported and no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem, since the check needs a parsed instant

criteria.given: a request WR-1 missing equipmentId and also dated in the future
criteria.then: both problems are reported for that input index, the existing field-order problems first and SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP last, and the validate trace note is the index-free "WR-1 rejected: missing equipmentId, future requestedAt" (label "Request without id" when the id is blank), with notes still sorted and out counting only accepted requests

criteria.given: a batch with identical content in a past-dated and a future-dated request, processed by WorkRequestProcessor with a fixed clock
criteria.when: process(batch) runs and the batch is shuffled repeatedly
criteria.then: the future-dated request is rejected in validate, never reaches deduplicate (no DUPLICATE problem or escalation for it), the trace still has exactly three entries validate/deduplicate/prioritize, and queue, problems and notes are identical for every ordering with SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problems ordered by inputIndex inside the validate block

the no-arg constructor still compiles and behaves as if given Clock.systemUTC(), a new WorkRequestValidator(Clock clock) overload exists that throws NullPointerException with message "clock" on null, and clock.instant() is read once per validate call so all requests in a batch share one instant

criteria.when: it starts with no overriding bean
criteria.then: ProcessingConfig exposes a java.time.Clock bean named clock returning Clock.systemUTC() and builds the workRequestValidator bean with it

criteria.given: the pinned 13-request sample batch (all requestedAt on 2026-10-20) and the generated order-independence batch
criteria.when: they are processed after 2026-10-20 with the system clock
criteria.then: the sample batch produces no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP and keeps its pinned queue, problems and counts 13 → 10 → 6, while the generated batch is extended to include a future-dated request so every ProblemCode value, including SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP, is still covered and BatchObserver reports one counter per code

outOfScope: Any configurable clock-skew tolerance or app.* property for the future check
Making DuplicateResolver, WorkRequestSorter or WorkRequestProcessor clock-aware
Changing the pinned sample-batch.json data or its expected output
Changing the API DTO shape or adding a new HTTP endpoint/response field
Changing existing ProblemCode constant order or existing problem messages
